author: Mohammad Yeasin
subject: grammar
title: Present Simple Tense
intro_blurb: The Present Simple Tense is one of the most important English grammar topics. It is used in IELTS, BCS, bank exams, spoken English, and everyday conversations. In this lesson, you will learn the rules, Bangla explanation, examples, common mistakes, and practice exercises.
learning_outcomes: Understand when to use the Present Simple Tense
Form positive, negative, and question sentences
Apply the tense in real-life conversations

timeline.description: I work in Dhaka every day. (habitual action that repeats regularly)

comparison.usage: Completed actions at a specific time in the past

common_mistakes.explanation: For He/She/It, add 's' or 'es' to the verb.
Use Past Simple for yesterday, not Present Simple.

audio_examples: They do not play cricket on Sundays.
speaking_practice: I walk to work every day.
She reads the newspaper in the morning.
They visit their grandmother every weekend.

quiz.question: Which is the correct sentence?
quiz.explanation: For He/She/It, add 's' to the verb.

quiz.question: Fill in the blank: He _____ (watch) TV every evening.
Correct the sentence: She always drink tea.
Translate to English: আমি প্রতিদিন সকাল ৬টায় উঠি।
quiz.answer: I get up at 6 am every day.

faq.q: Why do we use the Present Simple?
faq.a: For habits, general facts, and daily routines.

faq.q: What is the difference between Present Simple and Past Simple?
faq.a: Present Simple is for routines and facts; Past Simple is for completed actions in the past.
Use 'do' for I/You/We/They, and 'does' for He/She/It.

faq.q: Can I use 'yesterday' with Present Simple?
faq.a: No, 'yesterday' is for Past Simple. Use Present Simple for habits, not for specific past events.

faq.q: What are common signal words for Present Simple?
faq.a: Always, usually, often, sometimes, never, every day, on Mondays, etc.
